title: Merge Triplets to Form Target Triplet
statement: You get a list of triplets (three numbers each) and a target triplet. You may merge any two triplets into one that keeps the larger value in each slot, as often as you like. Can you end up with a triplet equal to the target?

example.caption: Skip [1, 8, 4], which is too big in the middle. Merging [2, 5, 3] and [1, 7, 5] gives [2, 7, 5].

idea.sentence: Throw away every triplet that is bigger than the target in any slot. If the rest can hit each target slot at least once, merging them gives the target.

jargon.plain: One of the three positions in a triplet: first, second or third.
Take the larger value in each slot of two triplets. Values only ever go up.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: a list of triplets, then the target, e.g. [[2,5,3],[1,8,4],[1,7,5]], [2,7,5]

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Merge every possible subset and compare with the target.

rows.name: Filter and match
rows.note: Each triplet is tested once against the target and three flags.

fast.takeaway: Merging only raises values, so a too-big triplet is poison and every other triplet is harmless. Merge all the harmless ones and look at the result.

stages.title: Three flags
stages.note: One flag per slot: does some usable triplet equal the target there?

stages.title: Discard too-big triplets
stages.note: If a triplet exceeds the target in any slot, skip it. Merging it would spoil that slot for good.

stages.title: Mark matched slots
stages.note: For a usable triplet, any slot equal to the target is matched. Other slots are lower, so they cannot hurt.

stages.title: All flags set?
stages.note: If every slot is matched, merging the usable triplets gives the target exactly.

edges.title: Single exact triplet
edges.why: The one triplet already equals the target. All three slots match.

edges.title: Single triplet too big
edges.why: The 4 is above 3, so it is discarded. Nothing is left to match.

edges.title: One slot never hit
edges.why: Slot 1 needs a 2, but no usable triplet has one. A larger value cannot be lowered.

edges.title: Matches from different triplets
edges.why: Each triplet supplies a different slot. Merging all three combines them.

gotchas.text: A slot being lower than the target is fine, because merging can raise it. Only values above the target are fatal. Do not discard on a mismatch, only on exceeding.
Check the three slots across different triplets. A single triplet does not need to match everywhere.
Do not compare arrays with ===. [1, 2] === [1, 2] is false because they are different objects. Compare slot by slot.
A [3]bool array is a value type and starts all false. That is exactly what we want here, and no make or init is needed.

recap.key: Skip any triplet with a slot above the target. Among the rest, record which slots equal the target. All three slots matched means yes.
moves: Keep three flags, one per slot
Skip a triplet that exceeds the target anywhere
Set flag j if the triplet equals the target at slot j
Return true if all flags are set
